Scott Colom

Democratic candidate for United States Senate, Mississippi · Challenger

District Attorney, Mississippi 16th Circuit Court District

Scott Colom has been District Attorney for Mississippi's 16th Circuit Court District (Lowndes, Oktibbeha, Clay and Noxubee counties) since January 2016. He announced his U.S. Senate campaign in 2025 and is the Democratic nominee. He is running against Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Colom stands

Taxes
Proposes eliminating federal income tax for teachers and police officers who earn under $75,000 a year. He cites retention problems in both professions.
Economy and cost of living
Says he is running to fight for higher wages and lower costs for Mississippians.
Health care and hospitals
Says he will work to save Mississippi's health care and hospitals. He lists health care access as a central issue of his campaign.
Constituent access
Pledges to hold regular contact with constituents, including town halls, if elected. He says Hyde-Smith has not held a town hall in six years.

Background

  • District Attorney, Mississippi 16th Circuit Court District, 2016–present (elected 2015, defeating 27-year incumbent Forrest Allgood)
  • Attorney
  • B.A., Millsaps College
  • J.D., University of Wisconsin–Madison
  • Born December 24, 1982, in Columbus, Mississippi
